Many times this system is abandoned in the second week. Choosing well between the task management apps available today makes a real difference. You can make it to the end of the month with everything delivered on time, or discover late that you forgot a client. The good news is that as a freelancer, you don't need a complicated corporate system. You need something simple, free or almost free, and easy to update from your cell phone.

es->en:Antes de elegir, vale la pena def: Before choosing, it is worth defining what the bare minimum is. What in English is known as [[T0]], or task management, does not need to be complicated for a freelancer. If you work alone or with one or two collaborators, you do not need corporate reports or approval flows. The important thing is that the app has a useful free plan. It should also synchronize well between cell phone and computer. In addition, it should allow you to set dates and reminders without friction. With those filters in mind, two task management apps tend to stand out: Todoist and Trello.
es->en:Todoist se enfoca en listas de ta: Todoist focuses on natural language to-do lists. You write “call Ana tomorrow at 3pm” and the app understands the date and time on its own. Their free plan allows up to 5 active projects, 3 custom filter views, and one week of history. For a freelancer who handles a few clients at a time, this is usually enough. If you need more projects, advanced filters, or full history, the Pro plan is around $5 per month. It is one of the simplest task management apps in this comparison. It's a better fit if you prefer lists and reminders, not visual boards.

es->en:Si ya conoces Trello por nuestra: If you already know Trello from our [[T0]], you will know that it organizes work in kanban boards. Use columns and cards to show the progress of each task. For a freelancer, this helps you see what stage each project is in: “to be quoted”, “in development”, “delivered” or “paid”. Their free plan has no time limit and is enough for one person. The main limit is 10 boards per workspace. Among visual task management apps, Trello is often clearer than a flat list.
es->en:Si tu trabajo también incluye doc: If your work also includes documenting processes or keeping notes from each client, see our comparison of [[T0]]. They are more complete tools that combine tasks, wikis and databases. They are also more complex than Todoist or Trello. Therefore, it only makes sense to take the leap if simple lists have already fallen short. Asana also has a reasonable free version. Still, it usually works better for teams than for a single person.

es->en:La automatización con IA funciona: AI automation works best when it starts with repetitive, reversible, and measurable tasks. The objective is not to automate everything, but to reduce manual work without losing quality, traceability or human control. These seven criteria help you decide which tool to evaluate and which process to leave for later.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]1. Elige un proceso q: [[T0]][[T1]]1. Choose a process that is already repeated[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Empieza por una tarea que ocurre: Start with a task that occurs frequently: sorting requests, summarizing a meeting, assigning a task, preparing a first draft, or updating a list. If the process changes every time, first document the flow before automating it.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]2. Define el resultad: [[T0]][[T1]]2. Defines the result that a person must pass[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:La IA puede sugerir un texto, res: The AI can suggest a text, summary or priority; a person must continue to approve decisions that affect prices, contracts, customers, payments or sensitive data. Establishes who reviews the result and what is done when the information is incomplete.
es->en:Antes de conectar información rea: Before connecting real customer information, validate the flow with anonymized examples. Review permissions, data location, subprocessors, and provider policy when the process includes sensitive information.
es->en:Una automatización útil debe redu: Useful automation should reduce time or errors without moving hidden work to the team. Record how long the process takes before and after, how many fixes it requires, and whether people actually use it.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]5. Revisa el encaje c: [[T0]][[T1]]5. Check the fit with your way of working[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Herramientas como ClickUp integra: Tools like ClickUp integrate tasks, documents, automations, dashboards, and AI capabilities within one workspace. Before migrating, check that its structure of projects, owners and permissions can represent your operation without forcing it.
es->en:Para ver ejemplos de capacidades,: For examples of capabilities, see the official [[T0]] documentation. Don't assume a feature is included in all plans or countries: confirm the current package before purchasing.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]6. Diseña una salida: [[T0]][[T1]]6. Design an exit and a review[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Todo flujo debe poder pausarse, c: Every flow must be able to be paused, corrected and audited. It keeps a reference of the original process, avoids depending on a single integration and defines who can modify rules, prompts and automations.
es->en:Prueba con un solo equipo, una ta: Test with a single team, one task and a defined period. When the result is consistent, replicate the flow. This way you avoid paying for a complex ecosystem before demonstrating operational value.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Convierte la evaluaci: [[T0]][[T1]]Convert the evaluation into a visible stream[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Antes de suscribirte a una plataf: Before subscribing to a platform, organize the process you want to automate in our [[T0]]. Document the trigger, responsible party, review, and expected outcome. That map becomes your list of requirements when comparing solutions.

es->en:Cada mes armas la misma factura p: Every month you create the same invoice for the same client, changing only the date. That repetitive work is exactly what you can eliminate. Automating recurring billing means setting up the template, frequency, and billing once, and letting the system do the rest. In fact, most billing platforms already include this feature, although few businesses activate it. Here are the concrete steps to stop issuing manual invoices every month. [[T0]] [[T1]]

es->en:La [[T0]] aplica cuando cobras el: The [[T0]] applies when you charge the same, or a similar, amount to the same client on a periodic basis. Think about a monthly subscription, a permanent mentorship or a maintenance service. If you already invoice like this, but you do it by hand every time, you are wasting time unnecessarily. We already reviewed the available e-invoicing options in our article on [[T1]]. Most of those platforms already support recurring billing. Therefore, before automating recurring billing in your business, confirm that your current tool includes this function.
es->en:[[T0]]Paso 1: elige una plataform: [[T0]]Step 1: Choose a platform with recurring billing[[T1]]
es->en:No todas las plataformas incluyen: Not all platforms include this feature in their cheapest plan. For example, FreshBooks only activates automatic recurring billing from their $43/month Plus plan. Before automating, confirm that your current plan actually includes this option. If it doesn't include it, check if it's worth upgrading. You can also change tools before continuing with the configuration. In fact, comparing two or three platforms before deciding avoids having to migrate the entire process later.
es->en:Entra a la sección de facturación: Enter the recurring billing section of your platform. Create a template with the fixed data: client, service, amount and currency. Leave blank only what changes each time, such as the invoice number. Check the template twice before saving it. An error here is automatically repeated on each future submission.
es->en:[[T0]]Paso 3: define la frecuenci: [[T0]]Step 3: define the frequency and charging method[[T1]]
es->en:Elige la frecuencia exacta: seman: Choose the exact frequency: weekly, monthly or annually, depending on your agreement with the client. It also defines the start date and, if applicable, the end date of the cycle. If your platform allows it, activate automatic payment with saved card. This way, the client does not have to approve each payment manually. Of course, confirm with your client before activating automatic charges, to avoid surprises.
es->en:Incluso con facturación recurrent: Even with active recurring billing, some customers pay late. Therefore, activate automatic reminders before and after the due date. Most platforms allow you to schedule two or three spaced reminders. This reduces the need to manually write to each overdue customer.
es->en:El error más frecuente es automat: The most common mistake is automating before confirming the exact amount with the client. Another common mistake is forgetting an end date, which generates indefinite charges that no one reviews. It also happens that some businesses activate automatic charging without notifying the customer, which generates complaints. Additionally, some businesses forget to review the template after a price change, and continue charging the previous amount for several months. Therefore, review each setting carefully before activating it completely. In short, an error in the template repeats itself, so it is advisable to detect it early.
es->en:Un consultor que cobra una mentor: A consultant who charges a fixed mentorship fee each month saves about an hour per month by automating their recurring billing. An agency with ten monthly maintenance clients saves significantly more, because it multiplies that savings for each client. A freelancer with only one recurring client may not notice that much of a difference. Therefore, the real benefit of automating grows depending on how many regular clients you bill each month.

es->en:Empieza simple: tres columnas alc: Start simple: three columns are enough for almost any team. Use To Do, In Progress, and Done as a starting point. Of course, you can add a Review column later if you really need it. However, avoid creating eight or ten columns from day one. A board with too many columns confuses more than it orders. es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Paso 2: crea las tarj: [[T0]][[T1]]Step 2: create the cards with the real tasks[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Cada tarjeta debe representar una: Each card should represent a single task, not an entire project. Write clear and specific titles, such as Send quote to customer X, not simply Sales. Add the deadline and responsible person directly to the card. Thus, anyone who opens the dashboard understands the real state without asking. On the other hand, avoid creating generic Miscellaneous Tasks type cards. These types of cards end up accumulating pending items without a date or owner, and no one ever moves them.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Paso 3: pon un límite: [[T0]][[T1]]Step 3: Set a limit on tasks in progress[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Un tablero útil hace visible el f: A useful board makes the flow visible and limits the work that is open at the same time. Adapt the names to your process:
es->en:[[T0]] si «En curso» se llena, no: [[T0]] if “In Progress” fills, do not open any more tasks; helps finish what you started. If “In Review” accumulates, the bottleneck may be in approval and not execution.
es->en:Este paso es el que más equipos s: This step is the one most teams skip when creating a Kanban board for the first time. Limit to 2 or 3 cards per person in the In Progress column. If someone already has 3 cards there, they shouldn't start a fourth. That simple rule prevents the entire team from half-working on ten things at once. In addition, it immediately makes visible where the bottleneck is. In fact, it's the main difference between a real Kanban board and a simple task list.
es->en:Una lista de tareas te dice qué f: A to-do list tells you what needs to be done. A Kanban board, on the other hand, shows you where each task is and who has it in their hands. That visibility is just what you lose when everything lives in a note or a group chat. Therefore, if your team is already more than 3 people, it is worth taking the leap. In fact, the team sometimes puts together the board with a lot of enthusiasm. But no one checks it after the first week. Therefore, it is advisable to assign a single person the task of remembering to update it daily. In short, a board only works if someone takes care of it to stay alive.

Second, you need your Password or your e.signature, depending on which tool you use to bill. Third, confirm your tax regime: the majority of freelancers are in Business and Professional Activities or RESICO. Without these three correct data, the system rejects the receipt or issues it with errors.

es->en:El SAT ofrece Factura Electrónica: The SAT offers Electronic Invoice in My Accounts, a free tool designed for individuals with low billing volume. There is also the Invoice SAT Móvil app, useful if you need to stamp a receipt from your cell phone. Therefore, for electronic invoicing in Mexico with a few clients per month, you do not need to hire any external software. Only if your volume grows a lot, or you need to automate the process, is it worth checking out private platforms with more features.

There you will find the form to issue your receipt. Therefore, save the direct link among your favorites, because you will use it every time you invoice.
es->en:Ingresa el RFC de tu cliente exac: Enter your client's RFC exactly as it appears on their tax certificate. Additionally, it describes the service provided clearly. Enter the amount before any applicable withholding. Also select the corresponding tax regime and use of CFDI. Therefore, ask your client for this information before starting the process, so as not to interrupt it halfway.
es->en:Revisa cada dato con cuidado ante: Review each information carefully before continuing. Once stamped, the CFDI cannot be edited directly. If you made a mistake, you will have to cancel it and issue a new one, which may require customer acceptance. Therefore, this verification step is the most important of the entire process. When you confirm that everything is correct, stamp the receipt. The system generates the XML and the PDF, and registers it with the SAT.

es->en:[[T0]] sigue siendo la versión vi: [[T0]] is still the current version, mandatory from 2023. Of course, there is a recent clarification that is worth knowing. The SAT confirmed that the printed Tax Status Certificate is no longer a legal requirement for a client to invoice you or for you to invoice. What must always match is your data: RFC, name and postal code, as stated in the SAT. Therefore, although you do not need the physical document, you do need that data to be correct and updated.
es->en:[[T0]]RESICO o Actividades Empres: [[T0]]RESICO or Business Activities: which regime suits you[[T1]]
es->en:RESICO aplica si tus ingresos anu: RESICO applies if your annual income does not exceed 3.5 million pesos. This regime does not allow deductions, but calculates the tax at a low rate on what was actually collected. The Business and Professional Activities Regime, on the other hand, does allow expenses to be deducted. Of course, a higher progressive rate applies. Therefore, if you have few deductible expenses, RESICO is usually better. If, on the other hand, you deduct equipment, office or tools on a regular basis, the traditional regime can save you more per year.

es->en:Antes de facturar como independie: Before billing as a freelancer in Peru, confirm three things. First, your RUC must be active, with a tax address in “existing” status. Second, you need your Sol Key, the password that gives you access to SUNAT's online procedures. Third, your RUC must have the fourth category income code enabled, 030401. Without that code, the system will not let you issue the receipt. If you have just obtained your RUC, review this requirement before attempting the first procedure.
es->en:[[T0]]SUNAT: la plataforma oficia: [[T0]]SUNAT: the official and free platform for invoicing[[T1]]
es->en:SUNAT ofrece su propio sistema de: SUNAT offers its own electronic issuance system at no cost, called SEE-SOL. It is the simplest option for most independents who are just starting out. There is also a SUNAT mobile app, useful if you need to issue a receipt from outside the office. Therefore, to bill as a freelancer in Peru, you do not need to hire any external software to start with. Only if your volume of clients grows a lot, or if you also sell products and need invoices, is it worth checking out private platforms with more functions.
es->en:Entra a www.sunat.gob.pe con tu R: Go to www.sunat.gob.pe with your RUC and your SOL Code. Look for the Companies route, then Payment Receipts, then SEE-SOL. There you will find the Receipt for Fees option. This first step is the same every time you issue a receipt, so it is a good idea to save the direct link among your browser favorites.
es->en:Ingresa el RUC o DNI de tu client: Enter your client's RUC or DNI, as appropriate. Then, describe the service provided clearly and specifically. Write the gross amount in soles, before any withholdings. Also select the correct type of rental, almost always fourth category for independent services. Therefore, have the client's information at hand before starting, so as not to interrupt the process halfway.
es->en:Revisa cada dato con cuidado ante: Review each information carefully before continuing. Once you issue the receipt, you cannot modify it. If you made a mistake, you will have to cancel it and issue a new one, which complicates your registration. Therefore, this verification step is the most important of the entire procedure. When you confirm that everything is correct, click Issue. The system generates the PDF and automatically registers it with SUNAT.
es->en:La retención del 8% aplica cuando: The 8% withholding applies when the receipt exceeds 1,500 soles and the client is a company or other agent obliged to withhold. For example, a receipt of 2,000 soles generates a withholding of 160 soles, and you receive 1,840 soles net. Of course, if you have an active withholding suspension, that rule does not apply. Therefore, it is a good idea to review each large receipt before agreeing on the final amount with the client.
es->en:[[T0]]Cómo solicitar la suspensió: [[T0]]How to request the suspension of withholdings[[T1]]
es->en:Si tus ingresos anuales como inde: If your annual income as an independent does not exceed 48,125 soles, or 4,010 soles per month, you can request the suspension of withholdings. The process is done from SUNAT Online Operations, in the option Request for Suspension of Fourth Category Withholdings. Once approved, your clients no longer withhold 8% on each payment. Therefore, if you work with few clients and moderate amounts, it is worth processing it at the beginning of each year.
es->en:[[T0]]Errores comunes al facturar: [[T0]]Common errors when billing as an independent in Peru[[T1]]
es->en:El error más frecuente es emitir: The most frequent error is issuing the receipt with the client's RUC written incorrectly, which forces it to be cancelled. Another common mistake is forgetting to process the suspension of withholdings, even if the income qualifies. It also happens that some independents describe the service so vaguely that it then complicates their own tax return. Therefore, be specific in the description from the first receipt. In short, checking each data twice saves a lot of time later.
es->en:Si emites pocos recibos al mes, e: If you issue a few receipts per month, SUNAT's free system covers everything you need. es->en:¿Llevas meses guardando cada clie: Have you been saving every client, every call and every sales opportunity for months in an Excel sheet that no one fully understands anymore? You are not alone. In fact, it is the most common starting point before making the jump to specialized software. Migrating from Excel to a CRM sounds more complicated than it really is, as long as you follow a clear order so as not to lose a single contact along the way. In this guide we explain, step by step, how to move your data safely, what mistakes to avoid and how to leave your information ready to work from day one. [[T0]]

es->en:Antes de migrar de Excel a un CRM: Before migrating from Excel to a CRM, it is important to be clear about what you are gaining. This tool, whose full name is Customer Relationship Management, centralizes each customer's history in one place. In addition, it prevents two people on the team from calling the same prospect on the same day, and automatically notifies when an opportunity has been without movement for too long. If you still have doubts about the concept, check out our guide on [[T0]].
es->en:Ahí explicamos con calma para qué: There we calmly explain what exactly this tool is for and how it differs from a traditional spreadsheet. Wikipedia, for its part, offers a [[T0]], useful if you want to delve deeper into the origin of the concept.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Antes de migrar: audi: [[T0]][[T1]]Before migrating: audit and clean your Excel file[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:La calidad de migrar de Excel a u: The quality of migrating from Excel to a CRM depends almost entirely on the quality of the source file. Therefore, before moving your data from Excel to a CRM, it is advisable to spend a full afternoon organizing the sheet. Eliminate empty rows and unify the phone and date formats (the platform will not interpret “02/01/2026” the same as “Feb-1-26”). Additionally, separate the full name into two columns—first name and last name—and check that there are no duplicate contacts with different data. Additionally, add a column with a unique identifier per customer. This way, if something goes wrong during the import, you'll be able to track exactly which record was lost or duplicated.

You upload the file, the system detects the columns automatically, and you confirm or correct the mapping before clicking “import”. If they do not match, check to see if any rows were discarded due to having empty or misspelled mail, as this is the most common reason for rejection. Then, randomly choose ten records and open them one by one to confirm that the customer's phone, company, and status arrived complete. Finally, define with your team an exact date from which Excel stops updating and this tool becomes the only source of truth.

es->en:Monday.com es un ejemplo de lo qu: Monday.com is an example of what is known in English as [[T0]], a category of platforms that goes beyond a simple task board. To understand if Monday.com is worth it, first look at everything it includes: spreadsheet views, timelines, dashboards with charts, and visual automations that are easy to set up without knowing how to code.
es->en:Está pensado sobre todo para equi: It is designed primarily for teams that already manage several processes in parallel, such as marketing, sales, and operations. These teams want to centralize everything on a single platform, instead of using a different tool for each area. For a freelancer or a team of two or three people with a single type of project, much of that power goes unused.
es->en:Aquí está el primer punto que hay: Here is the first point to be clear about before deciding if Monday.com is worth it: their paid plans do not charge per person. They require a minimum of 3 positions, so even a one-person team ends up paying as if there were three. This table summarizes the plans available in 2026:
es->en:Antes de decidir si Monday.com va: Before deciding if Monday.com is worth it for you, do the math: even the most basic plan already costs about $27 per month billed annually, considering the 3-seat minimum required. And that, before adding any advanced functions. For a team of 2 or 3 people who just need a simple task board, that amount can be hard to justify versus free alternatives like Trello.
es->en:[[T0]]Qué obtienes por el precio: [[T0]]What you get for the price vs free options[[T1]]
es->en:La diferencia real empieza a nota: The real difference begins to be noticed in larger teams. These include control panels (dashboards) that combine data from several dashboards at the same time, the most advanced automations that do allow multiple conditions, and native integrations with tools such as Salesforce, Excel and Slack without depending on external connectors. It also highlights its visual flexibility: you can switch between dashboard, calendar, timeline, or spreadsheet views without losing data. This is something that simpler tools like Trello don't offer natively. If your team already feels like it needs to cross-reference information between different projects, that's where Monday.com is worth it and begins to justify its cost.

es->en:Ya intentó organizarse con hojas: You've already tried to organize yourself with spreadsheets or free tools and left them aside due to lack of structure.

es->en:Si te preguntas si Monday.com val: If you're wondering if Monday.com is worth it for a skeleton crew, the answer is usually no. es->en:Cuando tu equipo dejó de comparti: When your team stops sharing the same office, coordination changes completely. What once passed for a quick conversation in the hallway now depends on information being in one place. Organizing a remote team with Trello is one of the simplest ways to achieve this. Turn that informal tracking into a visual dashboard that anyone can review, without having to ask “what are you up to?” by chat every two hours. In this guide we explain, step by step, how to structure boards and automate repetitive tasks. We also establish good practices so that a 100% remote team remains coordinated without unnecessary meetings. [[T0]]

es->en:Antes de pensar en automatizacion: Before thinking about automations or complicated rules, the first thing is to accept something: a Trello board replaces the visibility that the physical office previously provided. Anyone on the team, no matter what time zone they are in, should be able to open the dashboard and understand in seconds what is being done and who is responsible for what. This is especially important in [[T0]]. No one should have to rely on interrupting another person in chat just to know what stage a task is at. With clear columns and well-described cards, that question is already answered within the board itself, without the need to ask anything.
es->en:[[T0]]Cómo estructurar tu primer: [[T0]]How to structure your first board when organizing a remote team with Trello[[T1]]
es->en:Para organizar equipo remoto con: To organize remote team with Trello without getting lost along the way, start with a simple four-column structure: “Pending,” “In Progress,” “In Review,” and “Done.” Avoid creating too many columns from the beginning. A remote team just starting to use Trello often abandons the board if the structure is too complex from day one. Each card must have an assigned person in charge, a deadline and, if applicable, a checklist with the necessary steps to complete it. This is key in remote teams. Without that clarity within the card, any doubt turns into a chat message that interrupts someone else—just what a well-put together board should avoid.
es->en:Butler es el motor de automatizac: Butler is the automation engine that Trello brings, even in its free plan with 250 runs per month. It allows you to eliminate much of the manual work while organizing your remote team with Trello. For example, you can create a rule that automatically moves a card to “Under Review” as soon as the last box on its checklist is checked. Or one that assigns an automatic deadline when a card enters the “In progress” column. For a remote team, this reduces the number of manual steps someone has to remember to do. This is especially useful when team members work in different time zones, and someone isn't always awake to manually move cards.
es->en:La comunicación asíncrona es el o: Asynchronous communication is the other pillar of a well-organized remote team, and Trello helps if used with a few simple rules. First, write complete card descriptions, as if the person who is going to execute it will never be able to ask you anything in real time. Second, use card comments instead of moving the conversation to another chat, so that the context is documented in one place.
es->en:Por último, adjunta archivos dire: Finally, attach files directly to the card instead of sending them separately. These three practices, although simple, are the ones that are most forgotten when a team goes from working in person to working remotely. They are precisely what prevent the board from becoming useless after a few weeks.

es->en:Tu equipo tiene personas en Méxic: Your team has people in Mexico, Colombia and Spain, and scheduling a single meeting becomes a time zone puzzle. Therefore, achieving efficient distributed team meetings requires clear rules, not just good will. In fact, the problem is almost never the video calling tool. The real problem is the lack of a simple process that everyone follows. Here are concrete steps you can take from the next meeting, no matter how many time zones your team crosses. [[T0]]
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Por qué fallan las re: [[T0]][[T1]]Why meetings fail when the team is distributed[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Antes de aplicar cualquier truco,: Before applying any trick, understand the root of the problem. A poorly organized meeting costs time for the entire team, not just the person who called it. Therefore, the basis of efficient distributed team meetings is a repeatable process, not the memory of a single person. Additionally, the tool you use also matters. If you have not yet chosen a fixed video calling platform, check out our comparison of [[T0]]. There we compare price and limits of Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams.
es->en:Elige una zona horaria fija como: Choose a fixed time zone as a reference for the entire team, regardless of where each person is. For example, use the time of the city where most of the team lives. Communicate that reference in the shared calendar, not just in a single message. Thus, everyone calculates their own local time without confusion. On the other hand, avoid changing the reference every week. That only adds more confusion to an already complicated problem.
es->en:Define un rango de dos o tres hor: Define a range of two or three hours where the work days of the entire team coincide. Schedule the meetings there that really need everyone present. Outside of that window, avoid calling mandatory meetings. Of course, if a time zone is outside that range almost always, consider rotating shifts. Thus, the same group does not always have the most uncomfortable schedule.
es->en:Una reunión sin agenda tiende a e: A meeting without an agenda tends to drag on unnecessarily. Send the points to be treated at least a day before, not minutes before starting. It also asks that each person arrive with their contributions already thought out. That simple habit reduces the actual meeting time almost in half. Additionally, make it clear what the objective of the meeting is in a single sentence, at the beginning of the agenda.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Paso 4: graba las reu: [[T0]][[T1]]Step 4: Record meetings for those who cannot attend[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:En equipos distribuidos, alguien: In distributed teams, someone is always left outside the chosen schedule. Therefore, record the meeting and share it with those who could not connect live. Zoom and Google Meet allow recording directly from their paid plans. If your team already uses Microsoft Teams for daily chat, we review that option in depth in our [[T0]] comparison. Still, recording does not entirely replace live participation. Therefore, summarize key decisions in a separate message.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Errores comunes al or: [[T0]][[T1]]Common mistakes when organizing meetings with distributed teams[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:El error más frecuente es convoca: The most common mistake is calling meetings without verifying the local time of each participant. Another common mistake is dragging out the meeting because no one set a clear time limit. It also happens that a meeting is scheduled to resolve something that a chat message would have resolved just as well. So before sending the invitation, ask yourself if a live meeting is really necessary. Ultimately, many meetings can be replaced by a shared document or a [[T0]].
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Reuniones eficientes: [[T0]][[T1]]Efficient distributed team meetings: a real example[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Imagina un equipo con personas en: Imagine a team with people in Mexico City, Bogotá and Madrid. The common window between the three time zones barely lasts three hours a day. That team decided to reserve that window only for meetings that really need everyone present. The rest of the conversations move to written messages with a response expected within a day. That way, no one stays up late or gets up early just for a meeting that could have been a message. That simple adjustment cut total meeting time almost in half in just a few weeks.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Cómo medir si tus reu: [[T0]][[T1]]How to measure if your meetings are working[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:No basta con sentir que las reuni: It is not enough to feel that efficient distributed team meetings are already a reality in your team. Measure how much actual time meetings take up each week, and compare it to the time spent on focused work. If that balance tilts too much toward meetings, something needs to be adjusted. When you also need visibility into the hours worked by each remote person, it is advisable to add a dedicated tool. Therefore, we recommend that you review our guide on [[T0]]. There we cover how to provide transparency without falling into excessive surveillance.
es->en:Envía esta agenda antes de la reu: Send this agenda before the meeting and allow each participant to arrive with context. If a point has no responsible person or expected decision, it should probably go to an asynchronous document.

es->en:Envíala con suficiente antelación: Send it early enough for the team's time zone and update it if the goal changes or an urgent decision arises.
es->en:Una pregunta o resultado esperado: A question or expected result, the person responsible, the minimum context and the decision or action that should emerge from the conversation.
es->en:¿Qué hago con los temas que no ca: What do I do with the topics that don't fit?
es->en:Pásalos a un documento de pendien: Transfer them to a pending document with the person responsible and the date. Don't turn the meeting into an endless list of undecided issues.

All of this happens at the same time, and something is always lost along the way. Therefore, choosing between Slack vs Microsoft Teams is one of the first serious communication decisions. In fact, it becomes especially important in an SME that is growing rapidly. They both solve the same thing deep down. They centralize the team conversation in one place. However, they integrate differently with the tools you already use. That difference, more than the price, is usually what decides which one is best. [[T0]]

es->en:Antes de comparar Slack vs Micros: Before comparing Slack vs Microsoft Teams in depth, define what you really need.
es->en:Slack nació como chat de equipo,: Slack was born as a team chat, and it shows in every detail of its design. Their free plan retains 90 days of message history. In addition, it allows you to connect up to 10 external applications at no cost. That's enough for a small SME that has just tried the tool. The Pro plan costs $7.25 per user per month, billed annually. With it, history no longer has limits. Group meetings via video call are also unlocked.
es->en:El plan Business+ sube a 15 USD p: The Business+ plan goes up to $15 per user per month. Adds artificial intelligence features and more advanced security controls. On the other hand, if your team relies on a lot of external integrations, Slack has the advantage. It tends to connect to more CRM and support tools than Teams. That flexibility is just what attracts marketing and development teams.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Microsoft Teams: la o: [[T0]][[T1]]Microsoft Teams: the natural option if you already use Office[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:Microsoft Teams tiene sentido, so: Microsoft Teams makes sense, especially if your SMB already pays for Microsoft 365. The Business Basic plan costs $7 per user per month. Includes Teams along with web versions of Office and 1TB of storage. Its free plan allows meetings of up to 100 people. Of course, it has a limit of 60 minutes per session. It also includes 10GB of shared storage, plus 2GB personal storage per user.
es->en:Sin embargo, ese plan gratuito no: However, that free plan does not allow you to record meetings. For that, you need at least the Essentials plan, which costs $4 per user per month. If your SME already uses Word, Excel and Outlook on a daily basis, Teams has a clear advantage. The team doesn't have to learn a completely new tool from scratch. In fact, that almost zero learning curve is the main reason why many SMEs choose Teams without comparing too much.

es->en:No aplica (Slack no incluye Offic: Not applicable (Slack does not include Office)

es->en:Antes de decidir entre Slack vs M: Before deciding between Slack vs Microsoft Teams, check which tool your SMB already pays for email and documents. That answer usually outweighs any new features the other option offers. For example, paying for two separate subscriptions for email and chat rarely pays off.
es->en:El precio es solo una parte de la: Price is only part of the real decision. Also check how easy it is for your team to adopt the tool without lengthy training. Slack tends to feel more natural for young teams accustomed to messaging apps. Microsoft Teams, on the other hand, integrates better if the team already lives within the Office ecosystem. On the other hand, consider how many group video calls you need per week. Therefore, if there are few, either of the two is enough without problem. It is also worth reviewing administration controls. Teams typically offers more enterprise security options from the most basic paid plan. This matters especially if your SME handles sensitive customer data or signed contracts.
es->en:[[T0]][[T1]]Slack y Teams en la p: [[T0]][[T1]]Slack and Teams in practice: two different workflows[[T2]][[T3]]
es->en:En Slack, el trabajo gira alreded: In Slack, work revolves around topical channels, each with its own purpose. For example, a small team might have one channel per project, another for announcements, and another just for team banter. In Teams, however, each team has its own space. There are tabs for chat, files and meetings in the same place.
es->en:Esa estructura se siente más cerc: That structure feels closer to a shared folder than a loose chat. Neither approach is better in the abstract. It depends on how your team already organizes daily work. If your SME is just beginning to formalize processes, Teams imposes a little more order from the beginning. That's why some technical teams still prefer the freedom of Slack, even if they have Office available.
es->en:Si tu pyme ya paga Microsoft 365: If your SME already pays for Microsoft 365 for email, Teams is almost always cheaper overall. If you use Gmail or Google Workspace instead, Slack tends to integrate better. This way you avoid paying more for a Microsoft ecosystem that you don't use for anything else. When the team relies on a lot of external integrations, like CRM or support tickets, Slack still has the advantage. On the other hand, if you are looking to save on licenses by combining chat, documents and video calls in a single payment, Teams wins for total price. es->en:Ya decidiste que necesitas automa: You've already decided that you need to automate processes, but you don't know whether to start with Zapier or Make. The Zapier vs Make comparison almost always boils down to the same thing: simplicity versus flexibility. Here we delve into the real differences between the two, beyond the price of each plan. [[T0]]
es->en:[[T0]]Zapier y Make en una mirada: [[T0]]Zapier and Make in a quick look[[T1]]
es->en:Ya presentamos ambas plataformas: We already presented both platforms along with a third option in our [[T0]] comparison. Here we go into more detail in the Zapier vs Make debate. They are the two options that generate the most doubts among SMEs that are just starting to automate. Therefore, it is worth dedicating an entire article just to the two of them.
es->en:Zapier organiza cada automatizaci: Zapier organizes each automation as a linear sequence: a trigger and one or more actions. That simplicity makes it easy for almost anyone to put together their first flow in minutes. You don't need to see a complicated diagram. Additionally, Zapier Copilot allows you to describe what you want to automate in simple text. The tool puts together the flow for you. Of course, that same simplicity limits what you can build when the process becomes more complex. So with multiple conditions or alternative routes, Zapier starts to feel limited.
es->en:Make usa un editor visual de nodo: Make uses a visual editor of connected nodes, similar to a [[T0]]. This allows you to build conditional routes, loops and branches. Zapier doesn't handle that as well. Therefore, Make is best suited when your process has several conditions or steps that depend on each other. In return, that same editor requires more learning time at the beginning. Of course, this initial effort is paid only once, while complex flows are repeated every month.
es->en:Con un presupuesto similar, Make: With a similar budget, Make usually performs more operations than Zapier tasks. Make's Core plan, at $12 per month, delivers 10,000 operations. Zapier's Professional plan, at $19.99 per month, does not advertise a fixed number of tasks. Instead, it depends on the contracted plan and how many steps each flow has. However, an operation in Make is not always equivalent to a task in Zapier. Each platform counts usage differently. Therefore, the unit price comparison can be misleading. It's a good idea to check how each platform counts your actual usage before deciding just on the number on the price tag.
es->en:Antes de decidir entre Zapier vs: Before deciding between Zapier vs Make, put together a test flow on both with the free version. In fact, that practical test reveals better than any table which interface feels most natural to your team.
es->en:El precio no es la única variable: Price is not the only variable that matters in the Zapier vs Make debate. Review how many apps in your current stack integrate each platform. Not all of them cover the same tools. It's also a good idea to check how each one handles an error mid-flow. That directly affects your critical processes. On the other hand, think about how easy it is for someone else on the team to understand a flow you put together. That matters especially if you one day leave that role.
es->en:Un negocio que solo necesita mand: A business that only needs to send an email when a new form arrives solves that in Zapier in minutes. A company that needs to route an order based on three different conditions builds that with less friction in Make. Additionally, a team that already uses many unusual apps finds more native integrations in Zapier. Neither of them wins in the abstract. Therefore, the right decision depends on how many conditions and branches your actual process has.

es->en:Si tu equipo no tiene experiencia: If your team has no technical experience and your processes are simple, Zapier reduces initial friction. If, on the other hand, you already have processes with several conditions, Make performs more for the same budget. That especially applies if someone on the team is already comfortable with flowcharts. Therefore, if your specific goal is to automate repetitive administrative tasks, also review our guide on [[T0]].

Choosing well between Zoom vs Google Meet avoids just that kind of friction at the least opportune moment. es->en:Antes de comparar Zoom vs Google: Before comparing Zoom vs Google Meet, define what you use video calls for the most. If you meet primarily with external clients, connection stability outweighs any other function. If, on the other hand, the meetings are internal, integration with the rest of your tools matters more. We already covered that crossover with team chat in our [[T0]] comparison. That decision also influences which of these two video tools ends up winning for your SME.

es->en:Zoom sigue siendo la referencia c: Zoom continues to be the reference when it comes to meeting with external clients or suppliers. Their Basic plan is free, but limits group meetings to 40 minutes. The Pro plan costs $14.16 per user per month, billed annually. Eliminate the time limit and add up to 30 hours per meeting. In addition, it includes 10GB of cloud storage and unlimited use of the artificial intelligence assistant. The Business plan costs $18.33 per user per month. Raise the participant limit to 300 and add more advanced administration controls. Therefore, if your SME organizes webinars or large meetings, Zoom maintains an advantage over Google Meet.
es->en:Google Meet resulta la opción más: Google Meet is the most natural option if your SME already uses Gmail or Google Workspace for email. Its free version allows meetings with up to 100 participants. Of course, there is a limit of 60 minutes per group meeting. To remove that limit, you need a Google Workspace plan. The Business Starter plan, starting at $7 per user per month, already allows for longer meetings. On the other hand, the Business Standard plan, from 14 USD per user per month, increases the capacity to 150 participants. In addition, it does not require installing any program: everything works directly from the browser, without prior downloads.
es->en:Antes de decidir entre Zoom vs Go: Before deciding between Zoom vs Google Meet, calculate how many long group meetings your team hosts each week. If there are few, the free plan of either of the two is usually enough without paying more.
es->en:El precio no es la única variable: Price is not the only variable that matters when choosing between Zoom vs Google Meet. Also check the quality of the connection with participants who have unstable internet. Zoom tends to be better suited to weak connections thanks to its [[T0]]. Google Meet, on the other hand, has an advantage in direct integration with Calendar and Gmail. On the other hand, consider whether you need to record meetings in the cloud. Both tools allow it from their paid plans. Of course, neither of them requires long contracts, so trying before deciding is still a real option.

This makes it easier to schedule recurring meetings with the same internal team, especially if you already apply the steps in our guide on [[T0]]. However, neither approach is better in the abstract. It depends on whether you meet more with external people or with your own team. For this reason, some SMEs end up using both tools depending on the context of each meeting.
